Title: Launch of the Nursing Now Campaign in Uganda
NewsSummary: Sonam Alumnus spearheads launch of Nursing Now campaign in Uganda
NewsContent:
On 27 February 2018, Nursing Now held launch activities worldwide. However, the main launch happened in London and was attended by Professor Sharon Brownie (Dean of the Aga Khan University's School of Nursing and Midwifery East Africa [SONAM - EA]) among other high-profile guests.

During the event, Lord Crisp, co-chair of Nursing Now shared the significance of the launch to the healthcare community as well as some great news: "On behalf of Nursing Now supporters across the world I am delighted to welcome HRH The Duchess of Cambridge as our Patron. Our campaign aims to improve health globally by raising the profile and status of nurses worldwide - influencing policymakers and supporting nurses themselves to lead, learn and build a global movement."

The Africa launch of the campaign will take place on 22 March in Uganda, therefore, several healthcare policy-makers and leaders from the pearl of Africa attended the London launch. Some notable attendees were Dr Diana Atwiine (Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Health Uganda) and Catherine Odeke (Commissioner of Nursing, Uganda). Ms Odeke, a SONAM Uganda alumnus, spoke during the event in praise of the Nursing Now initiative, noting that it "...has come at the right time when nurses and midwives in Uganda need it more than ever."

With this event and the upcoming Africa launch of the same campaign in Uganda, Nursing Now will continue to forge ahead to advance the role of nursing in providing quality, essential healthcare.
